B9b-07-eye-image-formation-ray

Ray diagram of image formation in the human eye. Left side: an upright green mango tree as the object. Two straight light rays from the top of the tree and two from its base travel to the eye, cross as they are refracted at the cornea and lens, and meet on the retina at the back of the eye to form a small upside-down image of the tree. Show the eye in simplified side section with cornea, lens and retina. Add a yellow optic nerve leading from the back of the eye towards a small brain outline with the occipital lobe shaded.
B9b-08-eye-accommodation-ray

Two side-section diagrams of the eye one above the other, showing accommodation. Top panel titled distant object: parallel orange light rays from the left entering the eye, ciliary muscles shown relaxed, suspensory ligaments drawn as straight tight lines, the lens thin and flat, rays meeting on the retina. Bottom panel titled near object: diverging orange light rays from a small object close on the left, ciliary muscles shown contracted and bulging inwards, suspensory ligaments drawn as slightly wavy slack lines, the lens thick and rounded, rays meeting on the retina. Labels for each panel: ciliary muscle relaxed or ciliary muscle contracted, suspensory ligaments tight or suspensory ligaments slack, thin lens or thick lens, retina, light rays.
B9b-11-blind-spot-experiment

Illustration of the blind spot experiment. A white rectangular card with a black plus-shaped cross on the left and a solid black dot about 8 cm to the right, held at arm's length. Below or beside it, a simple top-view diagram of a head with the left eye closed and the right eye looking at the cross, with one dashed line from the cross to the fovea of the right eye and another dashed line from the dot entering the eye and landing exactly where the optic nerve leaves.
B9b-13-hearing-pathway-flowchart

Flow diagram of the pathway of sound through the ear. A row of eight simple, clearly separated icons connected by arrows from left to right, then continuing on a second row: sound waves drawn as curved lines, the pinna, the ear canal, the eardrum vibrating, the three ossicles in a chain, the oval window, the uncoiled cochlea drawn as a long tube with a basilar membrane and small hair cells, and the auditory nerve leading to a brain outline with the temporal lobe shaded.
B9b-15-concave-convex-ray

Two lenses side by side in side view with light rays. Left: a concave (diverging) lens, thin in the middle and thick at the edges, with three parallel orange rays entering from the left and spreading apart after passing through. Right: a convex (converging) lens, thick in the middle and thin at the edges, with three parallel orange rays entering from the left and meeting at a focal point after passing through.
B9b-16-myopia-correction-ray

Two side-section diagrams of a myopic (short-sighted) eye, one above the other. Top panel: an eyeball drawn slightly too long, parallel orange rays from a distant object entering and meeting at a point in front of the retina, then spreading again to give a blurred patch on the retina. Bottom panel: the same long eyeball with a concave lens placed in front of it; the parallel rays spread out slightly after the concave lens and then meet exactly on the retina.
B9b-17-hypermetropia-correction-ray

Two side-section diagrams of a hypermetropic (long-sighted) eye, one above the other. Top panel: an eyeball drawn slightly too short, diverging orange rays from a near object entering and heading to a meeting point behind the retina (shown with dashed lines continuing past the back of the eye), giving a blurred patch on the retina. Bottom panel: the same short eyeball with a convex lens placed in front of it; the rays are bent inwards by the convex lens and then meet exactly on the retina.
B9b-18-astigmatism-chart-ray

Two-part diagram about astigmatism. Left: an astigmatism test chart drawn as a half circle of straight black lines radiating like spokes from a centre point, as seen by a normal eye (all lines equally sharp and black). Right: the same chart as seen by an eye with astigmatism, with the vertical lines sharp and black and the horizontal and slanting lines blurred and grey. Below, a small drawing comparing a perfectly round cornea (like a football) with an unevenly curved cornea (like a rugby ball).
B9b-19-colour-vision-test-plate

An example colour vision test plate drawn in the general style of a dot test, not copied from any real published plate: a large circle filled with many small round dots of different sizes, most in shades of soft green, with a large number 7 made out of dots in shades of soft orange-red standing out in the middle. Beside it, the same circle as seen by a person with red-green colour blindness, where all the dots look similar muddy olive-brown and the number cannot be seen.
B9b-01-human-skin-anatomy

Vertical section through human skin as a sense organ. Show the epidermis on top (thin cornified layer of flat dead cells, granular layer, Malpighian layer with brown melanin dots), the thicker pale pink dermis below with wavy dermal papillae, and a yellow subcutaneous fat layer at the bottom. Include one hair in its follicle with a sebaceous gland and erector muscle, one coiled sweat gland with its duct opening at a pore, and red and blue capillaries. Draw the sense receptors clearly in purple, each attached to a thin yellow nerve fibre: free nerve endings reaching into the epidermis, an oval Meissner's corpuscle in a dermal papilla, a Merkel disc at the base of the epidermis, a large onion-like layered Pacinian corpuscle deep in the fat layer, a spindle-shaped Ruffini ending in the deep dermis, a small round Krause end bulb, and a network of nerve endings around the hair follicle.
B9b-02-olfactory-pathway-anatomy

Side view (sagittal section) of the human head showing the nose and the smell pathway. Show the nostril, nasal hairs, the nasal cavity with three curved turbinate bones, a curved arrow showing air flowing in and some swirling up to the roof, a small yellow patch of olfactory epithelium in the roof of the nasal cavity, the thin cribriform plate of bone above it, the olfactory bulb above that, and the olfactory tract leading back into the brain (cerebrum). Add a circular enlarged inset of the olfactory epithelium showing tall olfactory receptor cells with hair-like cilia projecting into a blue mucus layer, supporting cells between them, and nerve fibres passing up through holes in the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb.
B9b-03-tongue-papillae-taste-bud

Two-part diagram of the human tongue. Left: top view of the whole tongue in pink, showing the V-shaped row of large circumvallate papillae at the back, leaf-like foliate papillae on the back side edges, small red dot-like fungiform papillae scattered mostly at the tip and sides, and the rough surface of tiny filiform papillae. Right: an enlarged vertical section of one circumvallate papilla with its surrounding groove, and a further enlarged single onion-shaped taste bud set in the epithelium, showing the taste pore at the top, taste hairs (microvilli) poking into the pore, long taste cells in the centre, supporting cells around them, basal cells at the bottom and yellow sensory nerve fibres leaving from the base.
B9b-04-tongue-taste-map-comparison

Two tongue outlines side by side for comparison. Left tongue titled area labels in the old style: tip shaded pink, front sides shaded light blue, back sides shaded light green, back shaded light purple, each area plainly coloured with a big red cross mark in the corner of this panel to show it is outdated. Right tongue: the whole surface evenly speckled with small dots in all four colours plus orange mixed together, with a green tick mark in the corner. Labels for the left tongue: sweet (tip), salty (front sides), sour (back sides), bitter (back), old tongue map (outdated). Labels for the right tongue: all tastes detected all over, modern view.
B9b-05-external-eye-lacrimal-apparatus

Front view of a human eye with its accessory structures. Show the eyebrow, upper and lower eyelids with eyelashes, the white sclera, a dark brown iris and black pupil in the centre, the inner corner of the eye with the small tear duct opening, and a cut-away area above the outer corner showing the almond-shaped lachrymal (tear) gland with small ducts and blue arrows showing tears flowing across the eye towards the tear duct and down into the nose.
B9b-06-human-eyeball-horizontal-section

Horizontal (longitudinal) section through the human eyeball, viewed from above, front of the eye on the left. Show the tough white sclera forming the outer coat, continuing at the front as the transparent bulging cornea; the dark brown choroid inside the sclera; the pink retina lining the back; the ciliary body with ciliary muscles in a ring; suspensory ligaments as fine lines from the ciliary body to the edge of the biconvex transparent lens; the iris in front of the lens with the gap of the pupil; the small front chamber filled with pale blue aqueous humour; the large rear chamber filled with very pale blue jelly-like vitreous humour; a small pit (fovea) on the retina directly opposite the lens; the blind spot where the yellow optic nerve leaves the back of the eye slightly to one side; the conjunctiva over the front; and a few eye muscles attached to the sclera.
B9b-09-pupil-light-reflex

Two front views of a human eye side by side showing the pupil reflex. Left panel titled bright light: small sun icon, small pupil, the iris drawn with the circular muscle ring shaded darker to show contraction and the radial muscle lines thin. Right panel titled dim light: small moon icon, large pupil, radial muscle lines shaded darker and thicker to show contraction and the circular muscle ring thin. Brown iris.
B9b-10-retina-histology-rods-cones

Diagram of a small piece of the retina in section, with light arrows entering from the top. Show the layers: nerve fibres leading to the optic nerve at the top, a layer of nerve cells, then a row of photoreceptors at the bottom against the dark choroid. Draw tall thin rod cells in purple and shorter cone-shaped cone cells in three colours (red, green, blue) side by side, each connected upwards to nerve cells. Beside it, a small separate drawing of one rod and one cone enlarged, showing the outer segment with stacked discs, the cell body with nucleus, and the synaptic ending.
B9b-12-human-ear-anatomy

Vertical section through the human ear showing the outer, middle and inner ear, with each region lightly shaded in a different soft colour (outer ear peach, middle ear light blue, inner ear light green) separated by the eardrum and the oval window. Show the pinna, the external ear canal with tiny hairs and wax glands, the thin eardrum, the air-filled middle ear cavity with the three tiny ossicles in a chain (hammer-shaped malleus touching the eardrum, anvil-shaped incus, stirrup-shaped stapes fitting into the oval window), the round window below the oval window, the Eustachian tube running down to the throat, the coiled snail-like cochlea, the three semicircular canals at right angles with swellings (ampullae), the small vestibule with utriculus and sacculus, and the yellow auditory nerve leading to the brain. Skull bone around shown in pale grey.
